### Script

`ScriptElement` · `src/html.ts:373` · status: **held**

Code run by the page, in a script element. Its text must not end the element before its end: where it holds the opening of an end tag of script, in any case, a backslash comes before the slash, which the code reads the same.

Section: 4.12.1.3 Restrictions for contents of script elements · `https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/scripting.html#restrictions-for-contents-of-script-elements`

| `endTagOpen` | `</script` | What would end the element in its text |
| `escaped` | `<\/script` | The same text for the code, which no longer ends the element |
| `everyCase` | `gi` | Every occurrence, whatever its case |
| `commentOpen` | `<!--` | What would let a later start tag of a script swallow the end of the element |
| `commentEscaped` | `<\!--` | The same text for the code: a backslash before a character that needs none |

| Input | Writes | Checked |
|---|---|---|
| `"const s = \"</SCRIPT>\""` | `"<script>const s = \"<\\/script>\"</script>"` | held, read as HTML markup |

### CSS style sheets

`CssStyleSheets` · `src/html.ts:87` · status: **held**

CSS as Trame reads it, with tree-sitter's CSS grammar: the values written in a style sheet are its numbers, with their units, its colours and its texts. A property, a class, a keyword (flex, none), a variable are names, and so is the value an attribute selector matches, which the markup shares with the sheet as it shares a class. A url() and an

Grammar: [Grammar of CSS](packages.md#CssGrammar) `0.25.0` (`tree-sitter-css/tree-sitter-css.wasm`) · files `.css` · named `css` in bodies

<details><summary>values: The values written in a style sheet: a number with its unit, a colour, a text; a plain value that holds a digit, which is the rest of a number the grammar cut (12.5px/1.4 reads 12.5, then px/1.4), a variable aside</summary>

```scheme
(integer_value) @literal.number
(float_value) @literal.number
(color_value) @literal.text
(string_value) @literal.text
((plain_value) @literal.text (#match? @literal.text "[0-9]") (#not-match? @literal.text "^--"))
```

</details>

<details><summary>parts: What a text is made of: a colour, a plain value as written, the content of a quoted text and its escape sequences</summary>

```scheme
(color_value) @literal.part
((plain_value) @literal.part (#match? @literal.part "[0-9]") (#not-match? @literal.part "^--"))
(string_value (string_content) @literal.part)
(string_value (escape_sequence) @literal.escape)
```

</details>

<details><summary>names: What is written like a value but names something: the value an attribute selector matches</summary>

```scheme
(attribute_selector (string_value) @name)
```

</details>

<details><summary>declarations: What a sheet receives and gives: each variable it uses (var(--x)), each variable it declares (--x: …)</summary>

```scheme
((call_expression (function_name) @_function (arguments . (plain_value) @parameter)) (#eq? @_function "var"))
((declaration (property_name) @output) (#match? @output "^--"))
```

</details>

<details><summary>globals: What reaches outside the sheet: a resource loaded by its address, another sheet imported</summary>

```scheme
((call_expression (function_name) @global) (#eq? @global "url"))
(import_statement "@import" @global)
```

</details>

<details><summary>roles: The places that give a literal its role (syntax.LiteralRoles): the value of a property, an argument of a function, an operand of a calculation, a condition of a media query</summary>

```scheme
(declaration (_) @role.property)
(call_expression (function_name) @callee (arguments (_) @role.argument))
(call_expression (arguments (binary_expression (_) @role.arithmetic)))
(feature_query (_) @role.condition)
```

</details>

Escape sequences open with `\`; numeric: `\` then 1 to 6 digits in base 16 (one of "\r\n" " " "\t" "\n" "\r" "\f" after them belongs to it); otherwise the mark escapes the character that follows it.

| Code | Must read | Checked |
|---|---|---|
| `.a { margin: 0 -2px; color: #fff; }` | literals ["0","-2px","#fff"] · roles ["property value","property value","property value"] · values [0,"-2px","#fff"] | held |
| `.b[aria-pressed="true"] { top: calc(env(x, 0px) + 20px); }` | literals ["0px","20px"] · roles ["argument of env","arithmetic"] | held |
| `.c { font: 12.5px/1.4 var(--font, "A \"B\" \2014 C"); width: var(--w); }` | literals ["12.5","px/1.4","\"A \\\"B\\\" \\2014 C\""] · values [12.5,"px/1.4","A \"B\" —C"] | held |
| `@import url(theme.css); @media (max-width: 920px) { .d { flex: none; } } ` | literals ["920px"] · roles ["condition"] · globals ["@import","url"] | held |
| `.e { --gap: var(--space-md); margin: var(--gap) var(--edge, var(--gap)); }` | literals [] · parameters ["--space-md","--gap","--edge","--gap"] · outputs ["--gap"] | held |

<a id="HtmlMarkup"></a>

### HTML markup

`HtmlMarkup` · `src/html.ts:26` · status: **held**

HTML as Trame reads it, with tree-sitter's HTML grammar: the values written in markup are the values of its attributes and the texts of its elements, character references decoded. A class, an identifier, and the attributes that refer to an identifier name something that the style sheets and the scripts share with the markup: they are names. What a style or a script element holds is read in its own language. Named "html" in the graph.

Grammar: [Grammar of HTML](packages.md#HtmlGrammar) `0.23.2` (`tree-sitter-html/tree-sitter-html.wasm`) · files `.html` · named `html` in bodies

<details><summary>values: The values written in markup: the value of an attribute, quoted or not; a text; a character reference on its own, between two texts</summary>

```scheme
(quoted_attribute_value) @literal.text
(attribute (attribute_value) @literal.text)
(text) @literal.text
(entity) @literal.text
```

</details>

<details><summary>parts: What a value is made of: an attribute's value as written (its character references included: the grammar does not catch them apart there), a text, a character reference</summary>

```scheme
(attribute_value) @literal.part
(text) @literal.part
(entity) @literal.escape
```

</details>

<details><summary>names: What is written like a value but names something: a class, an identifier, an attribute that refers to an identifier</summary>

```scheme
((attribute (attribute_name) @_name) @name (#any-of? @_name "class" "id" "for" "aria-labelledby" "aria-describedby" "aria-controls"))
```

</details>

<details><summary>roles: The places that give a literal its role (syntax.LiteralRoles): the value of an attribute, the content of an element</summary>

```scheme
(attribute (quoted_attribute_value) @role.attribute)
(attribute (attribute_value) @role.attribute)
(element (text) @role.content)
(element (entity) @role.content)
```

</details>

Escape sequences open with `&`; named: `&amp;` "&", `&lt;` "<", `&gt;` ">", `&quot;` "\"", `&apos;` "'", `&nbsp;` "\u00a0"; numeric: `&#x` then digits in base 16 up to `;`, `&#X` then digits in base 16 up to `;`, `&#` then digits in base 10 up to `;`; a mark that opens no known sequence stands for itself.

| Code | Must read | Checked |
|---|---|---|
| `<a id="Goal" href="#Goal">Goal</a>` | literals ["\"#Goal\"","Goal"] · roles ["attribute value","content of an element"] · values ["#Goal","Goal"] | held |
| `<p title="a &amp; b &eacute;">T &lt; U &#x2192; V</p>` | literals ["\"a &amp; b &eacute;\"","T","&lt;","U","&#x2192;","V"] · values ["a & b &eacute;","T","<","U","→","V"] | held |
| `<button class="chip" aria-pressed="true" hidden>x</button>` | literals ["\"true\"","x"] · roles ["attribute value","content of an element"] | held |
| `<!DOCTYPE html> <style>.a { margin: 0 }</style> <script>const x = 1</script> ` | literals [] | held |
